 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-11-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was pillion rider and her husband J.
Narayanachar was riding the TVS XL Super motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9059,
from Hosakote Taluk to Begur Devanahalli via Southegowdanahalli in a moderate speed, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached Southegowdanahalli, Devanahalli-Sulibele road, Devanahalli, at that time the driver of the Baleno car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525, rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without following any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the TVS XL Super of the petitioner from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient and later she took treatment as an in-patient in Baptist Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and maid servant and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.

The Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car Radhamma vs Mare Gowda K on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183799478/
2 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.3 is the insured of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
Whereas, the respondent No.3 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.3 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, he is the registered owner of the car bearing No.KA-03-ND-0525 and the said car was insured with respondent No.2 vide policy No.140522323110083027, valid from 12-07-2023 to 11-07-2024.
As such, if there is any liability, the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the driver of the said car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said car.

Further it is contended that,
the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-HD-9059, as he was riding the same without observing traffic rules and regulations and without knowing driving.
If he had taken little care the accident could have been avoided.
The rider of said motorcycle is the solely responsible for the alleged accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of insured car.

He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner,
injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.

He has contended that,
the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

For the above denials and contentions,
he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-03-ND-0525 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to carelessness and self negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9029, as he was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, without holding driving licence and without wearing head guard.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
The respondents No.1 and 3 have not intimated the respondent No.2 insurance company with regard to transfer of registration certificate of insured vehicle.
Hence, they both have knowingfully violated the policy conditions by allowing the person not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
On this ground alone the claim petition is liable to dismissed against this respondent.
It has denied the mode and occurrence of the accident and also involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA-03-ND-0525 as mentioned in the claim petition.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 17-11-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Baleno Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03- ND-0525 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 17-11-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider on TVS XL Super motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9059,
the same being ridden by her husband in a moderate speed, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when they reached Southegowdanahalli, Devanahalli-Sulibele road, Devanahalli, at that time the driver of offending Baleno car bearing Reg. Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and maid servant and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.

Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got Radhamma vs Mare Gowda K on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183799478/

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.10 to 16, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and dashing the same to ongoing motorcycle of the petitioner from the back side.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-ND-0525 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the insured of offending vehicle/Respondent No.3, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1/owner and respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9059 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525.
Further it is contended that, the rider of motorcycle has himself dashed his motorcycle to car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and caused the accident.

But,
the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to establish the said contentions.
They have neither adduced any oral evidence, nor they have produced any documentary evidence to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9059 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the Ex.P.13 sketch and Ex.P.14 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 20 feet wide Devanahalli-Hoskote road, near Southegowdanahalli Village, Devanahalli Town, Bengaluru District, in between the offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-ND-0525 and ongoing motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HD-9059 of the petitioner.

Further,
as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.15, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.12 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 case-sheet, Ex.P.4 inpatient records, Ex.P.5 clinical notes, Ex.P.7 neuro-psychological assessment report, Ex.P.8 MRI report, Ex.P.9 MRI films,
Ex.P.16 wound certificate and Ex.P.17 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered acute SAH in bilateral frontoparietal cortical sulci, acute intraventicular haemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-11-2023 at about 7:30 p.m., on Devanahalli-Hoskote road, near Southegowdanahalli Village, Devanahalli Town, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-ND-0525.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ND-0525 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained acute SAH in bilateral frontoparietal cortical sulci, acute intraventicular haemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
20. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.19.
As per Ex.P.19, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1992.
The accident has taken place on 17-11-2023 at about 7.30 P.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 32 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered acute SAH in bilateral frontoparietal cortical sulci, acute intraventicular haemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury and for the said injuries the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical impairment due to neurological conditions to the extent of 65%.

The Ex.P.3 case-sheet, Ex.P.4 inpatient records, Ex.P.5 clinical notes, Ex.P.7 neuro-psychological assessment report, Ex.P.8 MRI report, Ex.P.9 MRI films, Ex.P.16 wound certificate and Ex.P.17 discharge summary also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries.

The P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 17-11-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 30-05-2025, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further he has admitted that, while assessing a disability of a patient with respect to neurological disability it is necessary to consider multi disciplinary approach system, in multi disciplinary approach system the opinion of the neurosurgeon, neuro psychologist and neuro psychiatric is required, he has not obtained the opinion of the neuro psychiatric.

Further he has admitted that, the cognitive disability is assessed by a neuro psychiatrist or neuro psychologist, the neuro behavioral disability is to be assessed by neuro psychiatrist or neuro psychologist, he has not obtained the opinion from Neuro Rehabilitation Center.
Further he has clearly admitted that, Dr. Prathibha Sharan has assessed both cognitive Radhamma vs Mare Gowda K on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183799478/
7 disability and neuro behavioral disability, medical board is a competent authority to issue disability certificate in respect of neurological deficit and he is not a member of any medical board.

Further he has admitted that, the disability assessed by Dr. Prathiba Sharan at 45% is with respect to cognitive and neuro behavioral disability, the remaining 40% is motor system disability assessed by him.
Further he has admitted that, he had not obtained the opinion of orthopedic surgeon while assessing motor system disability.

Further he has admitted that, at the time of discharge from the hospital the condition of the petitioner was improved, after undergoing follow-up treatment as an out-patient the condition of the petitioner was further more improved.

Therefore, in the light of above noted admissions in the evidence of P.W.2 and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment, present condition of the petitioner and the oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the permanent physical disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the permanent physical disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

21. The P.W.3, who is the husband of petitioner, has deposed in his evidence that, before accident the petitioner was working in garment factory and also as a maid servant under different persons and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries the petitioner has become permanently disabled and thereby she has lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

The petitioner has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working in garment factory and also as a maid servant under different persons and she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to draw adverse inference against the petitioner and hold that, the petitioner has failed to prove her avocation and income and consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.
22.

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 32 years is 16.

Therefore, loss of future income is total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,92,000 X 40/100 X 16 = Rs.12,28,800/-.

Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.8,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 64 medical bills, as per Ex.P.18.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.4,92,195/- towards medical expenses.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,92,195/- towards her medical expenses.
24.
Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., acute SAH in bilateral frontoparietal cortical sulci, acute intraventicular haemorrhage and diffuse axonal Radhamma vs Mare Gowda K on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183799478/
8 injury and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 33 days, from 17-11-2023 to 21- 11-2023 and 21-11-2023 to 19-12-2023, in Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and Bangalore Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2 the said injury has caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injury sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
25. Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 33 days in Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and Bangalore Baptist Hospital,
Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

The P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, he has spent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards attendant charges, transportation and other incidental charges of the petitioner.

Further,
the P.W.4, who is said to be appointed as care taker of the petitioner, has deposed in her evidence that, since from the date of accident till today she is taking care of the petitioner, who has become mentally unsound and not able carryout her day today activities independently and for the said work she is been paid Rs.20,000/- per month by the husband of petitioner.
But, neither the P.W.3 nor the P.W.4 have produced any supporting document to show that, the P.W.3 is paying Rs.20,000/- per month to P.W.4.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the nature of injuries caused to the petitioner in the accident in question, treatment undergone by the petitioner and the period of treatment, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards the attendant charges of the petitioner would be justified.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards attendant charges of the petitioner.
26. Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 33 days in Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and Bangalore Baptist Hospital,
Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 33 = Rs.26,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
27. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Aralamallige Village, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bengaluru Rural, the accident has taken place on Devanahalli-Hoskote road, near Southegowdanahalli Village, Devanahalli Town, Bengaluru District and she has taken treatment at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and Bangalore Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of accident and the above hospitals, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
28. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 33 days as in-patient at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli and Bangalore Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 4 months and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.16,000 x 4 = Rs.64,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.

9 29.
Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 32 years and unfortunately she has sustained acute SAH in bilateral frontoparietal cortical sulci, acute intraventicular haemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 40% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.80,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
30. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo further treatment and it will cost about Rs.5,00,000/-.
But, he has not produced any document to establish the same.

The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence, nor she has produced any document to show that, she requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident and it will cost about Rs.5,00,000/-.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, nowhere in the evidence the P.W.2, who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of the disability suffered by the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner is in need of any further treatment.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court declines to award any compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses.

31. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 12,28,800-00 2.
Medical expenses 4,92,195-00 3. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 1,00,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 26,400-00 6. Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 64,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 80,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.21,01,395/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17.
